rules.description: In an uptrend, each of the last N bars has a small range and holds within a fraction of an ATR of the recent highest high -- the one- or two-bar 'high and tight flag' that is a complete pullback. Mirrored below the recent lowest low in a downtrend.
rules.pseudocode: allOf(i = 0..pullbackBars-1: (high[i]-low[i]) < smallBarAtrFraction*atr(atrLookback) AND (highest(high, swingLookback)[1] - low[i]) < nearAtrFraction*atr(atrLookback))

complexity.reason: an all-of-N loop over an ATR-scaled range test and an ATR-scaled distance to a shifted window extreme

catalog_match.note: that rule reads a small bar near the recent LOW with an up close (buying at support); this reads small bars near the recent HIGH on the long side, a SIDE EXCHANGE which decision 12 says is a separate rule, and it is an all-of-N run rather than one bar

rules.merge_notes: Level is the shifted window extreme per decision 7, not a pivot. Distance and bar size both in ATRs (shift test). Grimes gives no numbers; defaults chosen. Kept apart from ShallowPullbackFractionOfImpulse, which measures depth against the impulse instead of bar size.

rules.description: One or two with-trend bodies sit inside an otherwise against-trend run of bars -- the 'hidden' complex pullback that looks simple on the trading timeframe. Long side: between minOpposite and lookback-1 of the last N bars closed below their own open.
rules.pseudocode: countIf(close < open, lookback) >= minOpposite AND countIf(close < open, lookback) <= maxOpposite

complexity.reason: one CountIF over a window compared against two bounds

catalog_match.note: add a minOpposite input; the catalog rule already computes CountIF(Close < Open, lookback) and caps it, and a BAND is not that rule negated (the PullbackNearMissesEntryPrice / ShallowDipBelowPriorBarLow precedent)

rules.merge_notes: Two restatements, one test. G01-15 spells it as a down-close run split by one up-close bar, G06-28 as one or two with-trend candles mid-pullback; both reduce to a count band. RECORDED LOSS: the count does not require the with-trend bars to be contiguous or central.

rules.description: No climax bar of either direction printed in the last N bars. Stated positively; the per-placement negate toggle gives Grimes's block, 'do not enter pullbacks following potential climaxes'.
rules.pseudocode: noneOf(i = 0..climaxLookback-1: ClimaxBar(i))

complexity.reason: a bounded OR over the catalog's single-bar ClimaxBar test, one ATR accumulator in the hook

catalog_match.note: the window form: ClimaxBar fires on one bar, and 'no climax in the last N bars' cannot be built by negating a single placement of it. Follows PostGapFadeBlockWindow's construction exactly, including the positive statement

rules.merge_notes: Two restatements of one filter (ch3 'do not enter pullbacks following potential climaxes'; ch6 blocks the simple Pullback template but allows the complex one). Cool-off windows 10 both times. ConsecutiveClimaxBarCount is the count form and is not this.

rules.description: No momentum divergence at a price extreme fired in the last N bars -- Grimes's 'long trades should not be entered on the next pullback' after a divergence. Stated positively; negate the placement to block.
rules.pseudocode: noneOf(i = 0..sinceDivergenceBars-1: high[i] >= highest(high, divLookback)[i+1] AND osc[i] < highest(osc, divLookback)[i+1])

complexity.reason: a bounded OR over the divergence test, which itself needs the 3/10 oscillator series and two window maxima

catalog_match.note: same shape as NoClimaxBarInWindow over a different primitive

rules.merge_notes: Divergence is settled by decision 3 (window maxima on the 3/10 oscillator, key MomentumDivergenceAtSwingExtreme), so this is B, not C. The window OR is what a single negated placement of that rule cannot express.

rules.description: A short net directional move that is large relative to recent volatility: somewhere within the last searchBars bars, the close moved more than K ATRs over legBars bars. Grimes's 'impulse move' / 'momentum move', and the with-trend precondition for trading a pullback.
rules.pseudocode: anyOf(i = 0..searchBars: close[i] - close[i+legBars] > impulseAtrMult * atr(atrLength)[i])

complexity.reason: a fixed-offset net-move comparison against an ATR, optionally scanned back over a small window

catalog_match.note: Momentum compares close with close N bars ago against zero; this adds an ATR-scaled threshold and a search window, so it fires on a far smaller set of bars. Not EmaSlope (the EMA against its own past value), not StrongTrendBarRun (per-bar bodies, no net-move term)

rules.merge_notes: G16-09 is the bar-0 test; G03-15 ('trade only pullbacks preceded by significant momentum', 15 bars) is the same test as a window, carried as searchBars rather than a second rule. G03-15's oscillator-extreme spelling loses to the price form on mechanizability; the oscillator rule lives in indicators_bands.

rules.description: Grimes's pullback primitive: a countertrend move inside a trend that has not yet produced a new extreme in the countertrend direction. The book deliberately declines a numeric boundary and says flag / pennant / box are not meaningful distinctions.
rules.pseudocode: legHigh - low[0] >= retracementFraction * (legHigh - legLow), legHigh/legLow over the last N bars including this one

complexity.reason: two window extremes and one multiplication

catalog_match.note: the depth reading at a small fraction. The corpus already carries the whole primitive: depth is PullbackDepthFromRecentHigh, duration is PullbackDurationBars, leg count is HighLowBarCount / LegCountAtLeast, 'no new extreme for N bars' is BarsSinceExtremeExceeds

rules.merge_notes: DO NOT AUTHOR. Both sources are definitional; Grimes adds no threshold the corpus lacks. Recorded as a design decision so no later bucket re-raises 'what is a pullback'.

rules.description: The current pullback has completed two or more internal legs -- a complex ('two-legged') pullback rather than a simple one.
rules.pseudocode: legCount(currentPullback) >= minLegs

complexity.reason: needs the settled leg counter

catalog_match.note: identical: the settled counter read as a standing threshold, default minLegs 2

rules.merge_notes: Glossary restatement of the catalog rule. Grimes's swingStrength 2 matches the corpus pivot default but the catalog rule uses the settled bar counter, which is cheaper and already on disk.

rules.description: The ABCD complex pullback: after a first countertrend leg and a failed with-trend resumption, a second countertrend leg carries beyond the first leg's extreme.
rules.pseudocode: legCount >= 2 AND runningLowSinceLastCountedBar < lowRetainedWhenCountFirstReachedOne

complexity.reason: one latched price on top of the settled leg counter

catalog_match.note: same test, same construction; the catalog rule was mined from Brooks's expanding correction and states Grimes's ABCD exactly

rules.merge_notes: Two restatements (ch3 prose, ch6 ABCD lettering). The corpus rule's settled counter beats a fresh pivot sequence on mechanizability. Distinct from ComplexPullbackTwoLegs, which only counts legs and does not compare their extremes.

rules.description: The mean bar range over the pullback window is smaller than a fraction of the mean bar range over the setup leg immediately before it -- 'good pullbacks almost always show reduced activity'.
rules.pseudocode: average(high - low, pullbackBars) < reducedFraction * average(high - low, legBars)[pullbackBars]

complexity.reason: two adjacent window means of the high-low range

catalog_match.note: that rule nests a fast TrueRange mean inside a slow one (lookback vs lookback x slowFactor, same end bar); this compares two ADJACENT windows of the high-low range, so the setup leg is out of the pullback's own benchmark. Not BarRangeBelowAverageMultiple, which sizes ONE bar against a window mean

rules.merge_notes: Two restatements, one test; ch6's explicit two-window form wins over ch3's pivot-delimited phrasing (decision 7: windows, not pivots). Fractions 0.7 (ch3) and 0.75 (ch6); 0.75 default.

rules.description: The pullback stopped going anywhere: the span of the last N bars is well under the span of the N bars before them, so the pullback is turning into a flat trading range rather than resuming the trend.
rules.pseudocode: (highest(high, stallBars) - lowest(low, stallBars)) < stallFraction * (highest(high, stallBars)[stallBars] - lowest(low, stallBars)[stallBars])

complexity.reason: two adjacent fixed-length window spans

catalog_match.note: identical arithmetic (flagBars = stallBars, shrinkFraction = stallFraction); Grimes's 'fraction of the trend leg range' is the adjacent window, the standing substitution

rules.merge_notes: G03-23 adds a second term, 'no new trend extreme since the pullback began', which is the catalog's BarsSinceExtremeExceeds in its own pane -- panes AND, so it is not folded in. Decision 8 (RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple) is the ATR-scaled sibling and loses here, since Grimes scales to the prior leg.

rules.description: A bar gapped in the trend direction and the gap has not filled since: the lowest low of the last N bars is still above the pre-gap bar's high (long), mirrored on the short side.
rules.pseudocode: low[fillLookback] > high[fillLookback + 1] AND lowest(low, fillLookback) > high[fillLookback + 1]

complexity.reason: the TrueGapBar test at a fixed lag plus one window extreme

catalog_match.note: that rule's reference is the PRIOR SESSION'S CLOSE and it needs the session machinery; this one's is a BAR gap (TrueGapBar's whole-range non-overlap), so it works on any bar scale and is what Grimes asks on a daily chart. Not GapFilledExit, an Exit anchored to a scanned-for gap

rules.merge_notes: Grimes's test is 'are there gaps up that do not fill'. Mechanized with the gap bar at a FIXED lag rather than a backward scan, which keeps it a plain window rule; the scanned form is GapFilledExit's construction and is the recorded alternative.

rules.description: The last minRisingLows confirmed swing lows each sit above the one before -- pullbacks getting shallower into a level, Grimes's ascending-triangle accumulation. Short wants successively lower swing highs.
rules.pseudocode: swingLow(1) > swingLow(2) AND swingLow(2) > swingLow(3)

complexity.reason: needs three confirmed pivots of one series, the corpus's newest-first pivot scan

catalog_match.note: that rule compares occurrences 1 and 2; add a minRisingLows input (default 2, so every existing placement is unchanged) to extend it to occurrence 3, which is inside decision 14's three-pivot scan and is what TrendLineSlopeFlattening already reads

rules.merge_notes: The pattern's second half -- a flat ceiling while the lows rise -- is LevelTouchCount or Ledge in its own pane, not folded in. Grimes gives no swing count; 3 is the miner's default and the parameterization's point.

rules.description: Since the breakout, every bar's low has stayed at or above the level that was broken -- 'a clean pullback that holds outside the breakout level', the easiest breakout pullback to manage.
rules.pseudocode: lowest(low, barsSinceBreakout) >= breakoutLevel

complexity.reason: a bounded backward scan for the breakout bar plus a running extreme from it

catalog_match.note: that rule already requires the lowest low from the breakout bar to now to have held at or above the level; at scalpDistance 0 its distance term falls away and it IS this test. No new input needed

rules.merge_notes: DO NOT AUTHOR: an existing rule at a pinned input, not a new one. G05-13 phrases the window as since-ENTRY; the catalog's since-BREAKOUT scan is the mechanizable reading and needs no position state. PullbackBeyondBreakoutPoint is the opposite reading and is not this negated.

rules.description: The pullback resolves with a strong with-trend bar: the body is large against the recent average bar size, which Grimes reads as confirmation that the trend is resuming.
rules.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] AND (close[0] - open[0]) > bodyMultiple * average(high - low, lookback)[1]

complexity.reason: one body against one window mean

catalog_match.note: same shape at a different denominator: the catalog rule benchmarks the mean absolute BODY, Grimes the mean high-low RANGE. Mean body runs about 0.6 of mean range, so his bodyMultiple 1.0 on range is roughly bodyMultiple 1.6 on body -- the multiple absorbs the difference, and a near-duplicate file is not worth a second call site

rules.merge_notes: Recorded default 1.6 is the converted reading of Grimes's 1.0-times-average-range. Not BreakoutBarLargeBodyLargeRange, whose body term is against the bar's OWN range; not StrongTrendBar, which adds tail caps.

rules.description: The trend has already made more than maxLegs same-direction pushes since the last opposite-direction leg -- after which Grimes says the probability of pullback failure rises with every further leg.
rules.pseudocode: sameDirectionLegCount(pivotScan) > maxLegs

complexity.reason: counts with-trend legs across a pivot scan, which decision 14 caps at two legs per series

catalog_match.note: that counter counts legs of the CURRENT PULLBACK off the settled bar counter; this counts WITH-TREND pushes since the last countertrend leg, a different series and a different reset. ThreePushPattern is the fixed-count sibling at three

rules.merge_notes: Reachability caveat for the authoring pass: decision 14's newest-first scan gives two legs per series, so 'more than three' is best mechanized as ThreePushPattern ANDed with a further push, or as HighLowBarCount (saturates at 4) on the with-trend series. Grimes's threshold is three.

rules.description: The ATR stands more than K times its own N-bar average -- extremely high volatility going into a pullback, which Grimes reads as a climax/exhaustion warning that the pullback is likely to fail.
rules.pseudocode: atr(atrLookback) > atrMultiple * average(atr(atrLookback), lookback)

complexity.reason: an average of an ATR, already built

catalog_match.note: add an atrMultiple input, default 1.0 so every existing placement is unchanged; Grimes's 'extremely high' is the same comparison with a multiple on the right-hand side

rules.merge_notes: One new input on an on-disk rule. The zero-padded warm-up caveat in the catalog line still applies and the multiple makes it bite harder early, which is worth a note when the input is added.

rules.description: Successive trend lines through the confirmed pivots are getting STEEPER, not flatter -- a series of ever-steepening legs, which Grimes reads as a market priming for a parabolic blow-off.
rules.pseudocode: newSlope > steepenFraction * oldSlope AND oldSlope > 0

complexity.reason: three confirmed pivots and two slope quotients -- exactly the machinery already on disk

catalog_match.note: add a steepenSense boolean, default 0. Decision 12: the negate toggle gives 'not A', and negating that rule also negates its 'the older line rose' guard, so the steepening reading is not reachable from a placement -- but it is a one-line comparison flip on identical machinery, so it is an input rather than a second file

rules.merge_notes: Grimes gives no ratio; 1.25 is the suggested steepening default against the existing 0.8 flattening one. Both sides keep the sign handling the on-disk rule already has for two negative slopes.

rules.description: A sharp leg was immediately answered by an almost equally sharp leg the other way -- Grimes: a very high probability of an extended, low-edge consolidation, so block new entries.
rules.pseudocode: sign(leg1) != sign(leg2) AND abs(abs(leg1) - abs(leg2)) < similarityFraction * max(abs(leg1), abs(leg2)) AND leg2BarCount <= maxLegBars

complexity.reason: two consecutive legs measured in price off the pivot scan plus a magnitude comparison

catalog_match.note: that rule is the BAR-RUN form (a strong-trend-bar run answered by the opposite run) with no magnitude comparison; this is the LEG form with an explicit similarity test, reading the same A/B/C pivot prices LegOneEqualsLegTwoTarget already reads. Not OppositeLargeBarsInWindow, which needs only one large bar of each sign

rules.merge_notes: Expected use is negated, as a block. Grimes gives no similarity number; 0.25 is the miner's. Not ExpandingTrianglePattern, which needs both sides diverging over five pivots.

rules.description: The impulse-retracement-impulse unit measured in price: the leg running now is at least extensionRatio times the same-direction leg before it. Grimes's setup-leg strength test -- the leg that sets up a pullback should be at least as strong as the trend's previous legs.
rules.pseudocode: (close[0] - swingLow(1)) >= extensionRatio * (swingHigh(1) - swingLow(2))

complexity.reason: three confirmed pivots, occurrences 1 and 2 of both series, with the ordering guard LegOneEqualsLegTwoTarget already writes

catalog_match.note: that rule measures the last two legs in BARS and is direction-agnostic; this measures them in PRICE and compares them to each other, which is the claim Grimes actually makes ('gauging the strength of the extension leg')

rules.merge_notes: G06-14 asks for the setup leg against the AVERAGE of several prior legs; G16-21 against the first leg of the same unit. The two-leg form wins -- decision 14 caps the pivot scan at two legs per series, so an average over three is unreachable. Ratio 1.0 (both sources).

rules.description: The pullback has already tested its own support level three or more times -- Grimes says do not buy against that, it usually precedes a failure.
rules.pseudocode: countIf(low[i] within tolAtr*atr of level AND close[i] held above it, i = 1..lookback) >= minTouches

complexity.reason: a toleranced touch counter against a retained level

catalog_match.note: that rule IS the counter at minTouches 3, and its own catalog line records both readings (touches weaken the level, or prove it), with the placement's negate toggle picking Grimes's. No new input

rules.merge_notes: DO NOT AUTHOR. Grimes's second term, 'lower highs into support', is CountertrendRunInWindow or HigherLowCount's short side in its own pane; panes AND, so it is not folded in.

rules.description: Two or three consecutive bars inside the pullback share nearly the same high, and this bar closes above that shared high -- Grimes's precise entry timing inside a pullback.
rules.pseudocode: abs(high[1] - high[2]) <= tolTicks * tick AND close[0] > highest(high, equalBarsCount)[1]

complexity.reason: a small-window equality test plus one breakout comparison

catalog_match.note: that rule states the matching-extremes half alone and assigns the sides the other way (matching LOWS on the long side); this pairs matching HIGHS with a long breakout through them, a side exchange plus a trigger. Ledge is the anchored multi-bar form of the same flat level and is likewise not the trigger

rules.merge_notes: Kept whole like a crossing: the flat level and the close through it are one event, and no pane-AND pairs the HIGH-side level with the LONG trigger. Tolerance stays in TICKS, as MicroDoubleExtreme's does -- Grimes means literally equal highs.

rules.description: Grimes's first pullback trigger: the line bounding the pullback is penetrated and price recovers straight back across it. Mechanized as the previous bar trading below the pullback's shifted window low while this bar closes back above it.
rules.pseudocode: low[1] < lowest(low, pullbackLookback)[2] AND close[0] > lowest(low, pullbackLookback)[2]

complexity.reason: one shifted window extreme read on two bars

catalog_match.note: that rule's level is a CONFIRMED SWING PIVOT and its trigger is this bar taking out the prior bar's high by a tick; this one's level is the shifted window extreme (decision 7) and the recovery is this bar's CLOSE back above it, so the two fire on different bars. Not DipBelowPriorLowCloseBackAbove, whose level is the single prior bar's low and whose dip and recovery are the SAME bar

rules.merge_notes: Stray from breakouts. The book's trigger is a drawn trend line or channel line; the window-extreme proxy wins on mechanizability (decision 7) and needs no pivot retention. TrendLineBreak with decision 17's maxAnchorSpanBars is the projected-line alternative and is a different rule.

rules.description: The pullback has retraced between minFraction and maxFraction of the leg behind it -- Grimes expects terminations around 50 percent and anywhere in the 25 to 75 percent range, so both an unusually shallow and an unusually deep pullback fail.
rules.pseudocode: legHigh - low[0] >= minFraction * (legHigh - legLow) AND legHigh - low[0] <= maxFraction * (legHigh - legLow)

complexity.reason: two window extremes and two multiplications; written as products, so a zero-height leg cannot divide by zero

catalog_match.note: add a maxRetracementFraction input, default large enough to be inert so every existing placement is unchanged. A BAND is not that rule negated -- a pullback that never got near the leg fails this and passes the negation -- exactly the PullbackNearMissesEntryPrice / ShallowDipBelowPriorBarLow precedent

rules.merge_notes: Stray from swing_structure. Book values 25 / 50 / 75 percent; the band's edges are the defaults and 0.5 is the centre Grimes expects. DeepPullbackRetracementFilter measures the CLOSE over a shifted window and assigns the sides the other way, so it is not the host.

rules.description: The high-and-tight flag by DEPTH: after a sharp impulse leg the pullback gives back no more than a small fraction of it, holding near the impulse's extreme.
rules.pseudocode: legHigh - low[0] < shallowFraction * (legHigh - legLow)

complexity.reason: two window extremes and one multiplication

catalog_match.note: that rule NEGATED at retracementFraction 0.25 over a short window; its own catalog line names this reading ('negated, his strong-trend the pullbacks will all be small filter'). A plain negation, so no new file and no new input

rules.merge_notes: DO NOT AUTHOR. Kept apart from HighAndTightFlagSmallBarsNearExtreme, which tests BAR SIZE near the extreme rather than depth -- they fire on different bars and the authoring pass should compare them before placing both.

rules.description: Enter the FIRST pullback after a strong countertrend spike: a bar within the wait window dipped below its predecessor immediately after a run of strong trend bars, and this bar closes above that signal bar's high.
rules.pseudocode: exists j in 1..maxWaitBars: low[j] < low[j+1] AND strongTrendBarRun(spikeBars) ending at j+1 AND close[0] > high[j]

complexity.reason: a trigger against a bar at a variable lag

catalog_match.note: identical construction, including the oldest-qualifying-j rule that makes it the FIRST pullback; the catalog rule was mined from Brooks's high 1 after a spike and is exactly the Anti's trigger

rules.merge_notes: DO NOT AUTHOR. Grimes allows the support-bounce trigger as an alternative; that primitive (G06-04) sits in another bucket. G16-01's glossary Anti names this same rule.

rules.description: After a confirmed breakout, the first pullback ends and this bar closes back above the pullback's own highest high -- the standard pullback trigger applied post-breakout.
rules.pseudocode: breakout at bar k within maxBarsSinceBreakout, pullback of k-1 bars since, close[0] > highest(high, k-1)[1]

complexity.reason: a bounded backward scan with an open-coded per-candidate level

catalog_match.note: Brooks's three-stage breakout pullback, statement for statement: most recent breakout bar, a bounded pullback since, this bar closing through the pullback's extreme

rules.merge_notes: DO NOT AUTHOR. Grimes's own note -- 'it is really nothing more than a simple pullback trade' -- is why the corpus rule already covers it. The breakout-quality setup (G06-52) belongs to breakouts.

rules.description: The breakout pullback has traded back beyond the prebreakout base's own extreme -- Grimes: much more indicative of a failed breakout than of a pullback, so the trade is off.
rules.pseudocode: low[0] < levelBrokenByBreakoutBar, level extended back into the base

complexity.reason: a bounded backward scan with a variable-offset level

catalog_match.note: that rule IS this test, and its lookback input exists precisely to extend the level back into the spike: 1 is the breakout point, 2 takes in the breakout bar's own low, 3 the bar before that -- the prebreakout base. No new input

rules.merge_notes: DO NOT AUTHOR. Grimes states it as an exit and the catalog rule is an Entry-role filter, so an exit placement needs the Exit twin; flag that to the authoring pass rather than re-deriving the test.

rules.description: Do not buy a pullback that is far above the moving average: the close must be no more than K ATRs above the reference EMA, mirrored below it for shorts.
rules.pseudocode: close[0] <= ema(close, emaLength) + marginAtr * atr(atrLookback)

complexity.reason: an EMA and an ATR, compared as a difference

catalog_match.note: CloseBeyondEma at marginAtr 2.0, placed NEGATED -- a plain 'not A', which the per-placement toggle gives. Not CloseWithinAtrOfEma, whose band is SYMMETRIC: its own catalog line says the signed reading is CloseBeyondEma negated, not a rule

rules.merge_notes: DO NOT AUTHOR. The miner flagged the overlap itself. Grimes explicitly defers 'far away' to the trader, so marginAtr is the optimizer input the catalog rule already exposes.

rules.description: Grimes's named Pullback template (Buying Support / Shorting Resistance), the book's central trend-continuation trade: a strong setup leg, a quiet pullback that has not tested its support three times, entered on a break-and-recover of the pullback's extreme or on a bounce off it.
rules.pseudocode: ExtensionLegExceedsSetupLeg AND PullbackRangeBelowLegRange AND NOT PullbackSupportTestCount AND (LevelBreakAndRecover OR SupportResistanceBounceEntry)

complexity.reason: graded by its hardest part, the pivot-based setup-leg comparison

catalog_match.note: no catalog composite covers it; every part is a separate rule

rules.merge_notes: Carried as a named template per the brief. Grimes says flags, pennants, wedges and continuation triangles are functionally identical, so there are no per-shape rules. Stop and targets (G06-17/18/19) live in exits_stops and exits_targets.

rules.description: Grimes's named Pullback, Entering Lower Time Frame Breakout template: the same pullback setup, timed by a short-window breakout out of the pullback instead of by a bounce -- better momentum confirmation, worse trade location.
rules.pseudocode: ExtensionLegExceedsSetupLeg AND PullbackRangeBelowLegRange AND (LowerTimeFrameBreakoutEntry OR EqualHighsBreakout)

complexity.reason: inherits the pivot-based setup; the trigger itself is simple

catalog_match.note: the trigger half alone is close to HighestHighBreakout at a short lookback; the template is the pairing

rules.merge_notes: The lower timeframe is approximated by a 3-bar breakout on the same bars (decision 4's multiplier read downward); that primitive, G06-22, sits in breakouts. Stop choice (tight vs the preferred wider one) is exits_stops.

rules.description: Grimes's named Trading Complex Pullbacks template: the pullback has two countertrend legs (or the hidden with-trend-body cue), often after a climax where the simple Pullback template is blocked, entered on the same triggers.
rules.pseudocode: (SecondLegExceedsFirstLegExtreme OR HiddenComplexPullbackBodyCount) AND (LevelBreakAndRecover OR SupportResistanceBounceEntry)

complexity.reason: graded by the leg-structure part, which needs the settled leg counter

catalog_match.note: the two-leg part is the on-disk SecondLegExceedsFirstLegExtreme; the template is the pairing with a trigger

rules.merge_notes: Grimes pairs this with NoClimaxBarInWindow negated: a climax blocks the simple template but permits this one, which is the one place the two templates are not interchangeable. Target is the AB=CD leg-equality move, the on-disk LegOneEqualsLegTwoTarget.

rules.description: Grimes's named Anti template: after a pattern suggesting the trend could be ending, a countertrend swing emerges that is much stronger than the trend's previous countertrend swings, and the trade is the FIRST pullback after that swing -- entered in the direction of the new move.
rules.pseudocode: TrendTerminationPrecondition AND CountertrendSpikeStrongerThanPriorSwings, then FirstPullbackAfterSpike

complexity.reason: two pivot-based setup conditions ahead of an on-disk trigger

catalog_match.note: the catalog rule is the Anti's TRIGGER alone, with the spike defined by strong trend bars; the template adds the trend-termination precondition and the change-of-character swing test, which is what makes it countertrend rather than with-trend

rules.merge_notes: Grimes's PRICE-STRUCTURE Anti, the form he prefers; decision 6 leaves Raschke's stochastic original at C in indicators_bands. The setup parts G06-33 / G06-34 sit in climax_termination and swing_structure. The loose 'enter anywhere in the pullback' variant is dropped -- it has no bar test of its own.

rules.description: Grimes's named Breakouts, Entering on First Pullback Following template: a confirmed breakout, then the standard pullback trigger, with the prebreakout base's extreme as the extra invalidation level.
rules.pseudocode: BreakoutConfirmedByActivityBeyondLevel AND BreakoutPullbackEntry, invalidated by PullbackBeyondBreakoutPoint

complexity.reason: a thin wrapper over rules already on disk

catalog_match.note: every part is already authored: BreakoutPullbackEntry is the trade, PullbackBeyondBreakoutPoint the invalidation, SwingHighProfitTarget the conservative target, BarRangeAboveStd the breakout-quality gate

rules.merge_notes: DO NOT AUTHOR: a PLACEMENT RECIPE, not a rule -- the pane system composes it from four on-disk rules. Carried rather than dropped so the recipe survives for the template pass. Grimes: 'it is really nothing more than a simple pullback trade'.

dropped.reason: composition of RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple (the prior equilibrium) + BarRangeAtrMultiple (the impulse bar); the impulse half is carried as ImpulseLegNetMove
framework statement, no bar test: composition of EmaSlope + a pullback rule, both of which the chapter leaves abstract
composition of RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple + EmaSlope at 5x with the range's own slope opposed; decision 15 forbids re-raising the higher-timeframe read
composition of RangeWidthBelowAtrMultiple + EmaSlope at 5x agreeing with the prior trend (decisions 8 and 15)

sent to climax_termination and adjudicated there in the reconciliation pass: dropped as a composition of TrendRateAcceleration + BarRangeExceedsAverageMultiple + FreeBarOutsideKeltnerBand + CloseRangePositionRun + a >= 2 prior-leg count (LegCountAtLeast)
composition of HighestHighBreakout's short side (a new N-bar low of the pullback) + StrongTrendBar's short side

sent to breakouts and adjudicated there in the reconciliation pass: dropped as a composition of the breakout-failure signal (FailedBreakoutTemplate) + the pullback primitive in the new direction (decision 18)

sent to exits_stops and adjudicated there in the reconciliation pass: dropped as a composition of BreakevenStopAtRiskMultiple + the measured-move zone being reached and held, which ORed exit placements cannot express
sent to exits_stops and adjudicated there in the reconciliation pass: dropped under decision 24, partial profit taking is not expressible, so the partialProfitTaken state it needs does not exist

options: author a PullbackInProgress rule from Grimes's definition
treat the primitive as already on disk
design_decisions.recommended: Already on disk, do not author: depth is PullbackDepthFromRecentHigh, duration PullbackDurationBars, leg count HighLowBarCount / LegCountAtLeast, 'no new extreme for N bars' BarsSinceExtremeExceeds. Grimes deliberately gives no numeric boundary, so he adds nothing the corpus lacks; no later bucket should re-raise 'what is a pullback'.

design_decisions.topic: Band-shaped filters (a quantity with BOTH bounds)
options: a second rule file for the upper bound
a new input on the rule that already computes the quantity
design_decisions.recommended: A new input on the existing rule. A band is not the existing rule negated (a bar that never reaches the lower bound fails the band and passes the negation), and the corpus already keeps bands as first-class rules (PullbackNearMissesEntryPrice, ShallowDipBelowPriorBarLow). Four of this bucket's A-list are exactly this: maxRetracementFraction on PullbackDepthFromRecentHigh, minOpposite on OppositeBodyCountInWindow, minRisingLows on HigherSwingLow, atrMultiple on AtrAboveAverage. Every default is chosen inert so existing placements are unchanged.

design_decisions.topic: Grimes's pullback TRIGGER (trend-line failure and recover)
options: project a real trend line from pivots (TrendLineBreak plus decision 17's maxAnchorSpanBars)
break and recover of the pullback's shifted window extreme
design_decisions.recommended: The window-extreme proxy, key LevelBreakAndRecover: decision 7 already makes the shifted window extreme the default level, the proxy needs no pivot retention, and it is what both named templates use as their entry. The projected-line form stays available as TrendLineBreak and is a different rule, not this one at a parameter.

bucket_summary: 54 bucket candidates plus 2 strays collapsed to 33 rules, 12 drops and 2 cross-bucket sends (the reconciliation pass absorbed G02-05 and G06-25 into exits_stops rules and turned the other four sends into drops); no rule is blocked (zero C). The bucket is dominated by the Brooks-derived pullback family already on disk: 13 rules are D, of which 10 are outright catalog duplicates (the pullback primitive itself, the two complex-pullback forms, the breakout first-pullback entry and its invalidation, the Anti's trigger, the far-from-the-MA filter, the shallow-flag depth test, the support-test counter, the stall-into-range test). The A-list is 12: four are one-input parameterizations of on-disk rules (RetracementDepthWithinBand, HiddenComplexPullbackBodyCount, RisingSwingLowCount, AtrAboveAverageMultiple, plus TrendLineSlopeSteepening's sense flag), and the genuinely new ones are LevelBreakAndRecover, EqualHighsBreakout, ImpulseLegNetMove, PullbackRangeBelowLegRange, GapHoldsUnfilled and HighAndTightFlagSmallBarsNearExtreme. B carries the pivot-based leg comparisons (ExtensionLegExceedsSetupLeg, TrendLegCountAboveMax, OppositeLegsSimilarLength), the divergence cool-off, and the four named templates Pullback, PullbackLowerTimeframeBreakout, ComplexPullback and Anti.
